summary: Clean restack of two separately measured sliding-row wins on disjoint shapes. (A) applies to master's own blob d8769ef and (B) is gated away from every shape (A) touches, so each row is attributable from the profile and the PATH CHOSEN lines. Before the build: strip (B)'s kernel_fn try/except, prints and mutable set, and state the C=16 margin explicitly so the B=1 band is not silently gated off.
justification: A: The mechanism is plausible and was measured. Sliding verify_1 on master is FA3 main 7.9 + combine 3.9 + prepare_varlen 1.8 us + norm-gate (17.8 us shape). The s1 pseudo-decode kernel (grid p8, ticket) replaced that chain at 13.44 us in job 94523c33 on the exact master blob (d8769ef = BEST.submission_blob), so (A) is a re-run of measured code. Sliding decode_32 on master is _sliding_fused_kernel at 22.4 us (24.3 us shape, floor 3.3). Cluster C=4 measured 20.05 us in job 195dcc12; the Triton kernel it replaces is the same deep-splits kernel that is on master now. Each of the three rows has weight 46, and they sit in three different loads (decode 1, decode 32, verify 1), so the ~1.49x projection from substituting rows is arithmetically sound. The expected directions match the gates: full rows flat (byte-identical PSEUDO=false instantiations), sliding decode_16 flat (B=2..16 stays on Triton). Weakest link: the sliding decode_1 C=16 row. Its gain is 0.58 us (13.15 -> 12.57, 4.4%), and master's own sliding decode_1 has read 13.1-13.33 us across today's runs, so one run cannot confirm it. Worse, the hypothesis says gates route 'only when the printed interleaved graph-replay timing shows the new path winning by the stated margin' but never states (B)'s margin. If the builder reuses s1's >=1.05x, C=16 (about 1.046x) will usually fall back to Triton and the run silently measures master on that row. Second weakest: everything sits far above the 0.1-3.3 us floors, so there is headroom; the risk lies in the port, not the physics.
confounders: sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv: the cluster C=16/C=4 wins were measured against this exact Triton _sliding_fused_kernel, which is unchanged on master, so the comparison carries over. No confound beyond drift on the near-noise decode_1 row.
sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: the incumbent at sliding decode B=1 that C=16 replaces. Same code as in the stack run, so no interaction; the C=16 row stays near noise.

full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket: (A) adds a PSEUDO template flag and Lay<STAGES,256,true> to the same splitkv_attn_sk_kernel and builds with -DSK_PSEUDO=1. Full decode rows stay flat only if the landed instantiations are byte-identical (the sk_attrs IDENTICAL print must appear) and the landed-only rebuild fallback did not fire. A full-row move without IDENTICAL means the build changed, not the sliding work.

fused-preattention-triton: (A) keeps _pre_attention_kernel ahead of the pseudo kernel at verify B=1. (B) folds norm/RoPE/FP8 store into the cluster kernel at decode B=1 and B=17..32, with a K-byte encode that only matches master within rel 5e-2 (byte match is info only). That is inside the 8% cache bound, but a row failure on a new-cache test would come from this encode, not the attention.
interference: No companion is warranted. The two sub-changes route disjoint shapes, (A) to sliding verify B=1 and (B) to sliding decode B=1 and B=17..32, and each run is a separate graph replay. Each row's gain or loss therefore belongs to exactly one sub-change, readable from the profile's top kernel (splitkv_attn_sk_kernel<...PSEUDO> vs sliding_cluster_kernel) and the PATH CHOSEN lines. An ab-revert of a landed hypothesis would not change that: neither route depends on a landed tuning other than the incumbent each replaces, and those incumbents are unchanged since the source measurements. The only ambiguous row is sliding decode_1, and the in-run interleaved timing that the gate prints (cluster C=16 vs Triton, cold L2, empty-graph subtracted) already serves as its control at no check cost. The A/B partner restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn is already minted and covers the full decode_16/32 question, so no duplicate is queued. With 8 checks left and 8 queued, spending one on a control would be waste.
rules_flags: Porting (B) verbatim breaks the hypothesis's own kernel_fn rules. Branch stack-streamk-ticket-cluster-c16-c4's kernel_fn wraps _slide_forward in try/except RuntimeError, calls _slide_note (print) per call and adds to the module-level _SLIDE_NOTED set (per-call mutable Python state). Strip all three: decide and print routes once in prepare/import, and make kernel_fn a pure config-gated dispatch.

(B)'s _slide_self_check captures the graph and replays it once on the same inputs it ran eagerly (torch.equal(static, eager)). That does not satisfy the two-state rule. It must become: capture once, refill state A, replay, refill state B (different seq lens / cache_loc), replay, compare each to the fp32 reference. A mismatch there signals a pointer or buffer baked into the capture.

Audit (B)'s TU for any static/module buffer (the patch shows `static bool done[3]` at line 510 of the patch, apparently a host-side once-flag, plus _TICKETS in the sk part that master already has). Confirm that no device pointer, TMA map or state-sized workspace is cached. The cluster kernel's out is per-call torch.empty (shape-only), which is fine.

Timing-based gates are decided at import from measurements, not inputs, so they are rule-compliant. But they must be computed once and frozen before any judged call, with no re-timing inside kernel_fn.

Every-key check passes on the read code: the cluster kernel uses lo = max(0, seq - (window - 1)) with mask on every tile and asserts window <= 2048. The pseudo-decode path attends each of the 8 pseudo-rows' full causal window.
open_questions: What margin gates (B)'s bands? Recommend keeping (B) config-only as it ran in 195dcc12 (C=16 at B=1, C=4 at B=17..32) and only printing the interleaved timing. Failing that, set C=16's margin at <=1.02x, since 1.05x would drop the B=1 band at its measured 1.046x.

Compile budget: splitkv 49 s + sk 37 s + slide (fp8qk) 41 s + the -DSK_PSEUDO=1 rebuild, plus a possible landed-only rebuild fallback and an f16qk fallback build, plus all the gating timings. That is likely 3-5 min of the 15-min run. Print per-phase wall times. Is the torch extension cache warm on the judge?

Does the s1 IDENTICAL check (sk_attrs for landed variants) still print IDENTICAL when (B)'s TU is also loaded in the same process? Register pressure and smem attributes should not change, but the line must be in the log to read the full rows as flat.

The (B) self-check's cache tolerance is rel < 5e-2 with byte match as info only. Does the new-cache correctness bound (8% of the reference's) still pass on the kv_scale 0.015625 page-1 test? That test routes to master today (q_len 8 or page 64), so check that no cluster-gated test case has kv_scale != 1.
